full_judgment: 33. In distinguishing the decision pronounced by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Jibendra Kishore Achhara Chowdhury vs. The Province of East Pakistan. (1957) 9 DLR (SC) 21= PLD 1957 SC 9, Munir, C.J. observed that no analogy could be drawn between the impugned provisions of the Foreign Exchange Regulations Act and the provisions of the E. Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, whose constitutionality was challenged in the aforesaid case. The provisions of this Act which were impugned were held to be not unconstitutional as they had intended to eliminate all rent-receiving interests and to create a uniform class of tenants under the Government and that section 3 of the Act gave the power or discretion to acquire simultaneously or from time to time, the interests which were to be terminated.
